9293.inventory: Appendix B: MUST-1..69, SHLD-1..31, MAY-1..18, REC-1

input_classes.malformed: Bad frame/checksum/header/option extent; drop before TCP state mutation.
input_classes.state-inapplicable: Well-formed segment for another tuple or invalid sequence/ACK in this state; ignore or ACK/challenge by state.
input_classes.valid-unsupported: Well-formed optional offer or feature with no advertised semantics; structurally admit/ignore or decline without calling the format malformed.
input_classes.profile-limit: Valid traffic outside fixed segment/queue/owner/lifetime budgets; defined backpressure/reset/failure, not format corruption.

rows.title: Header and payload admission
rows.behavior: The data offset bounds a 20..60-byte header; payload starts after that header. Reserved received bits are ignored. No option walk exceeds 40 bytes.

rows.title: IPv4 TCP checksum
rows.behavior: The production sender checksums the IPv4 pseudo-header and segment. Both passive and active receive paths validate that checksum before tuple/state handling.

rows.title: Option structure and unknown kinds
rows.behavior: EOL/NOP, option extents and MSS shape are checked at byte alignment. Unknown well-formed length-bearing kinds are skipped; bad lengths and nonzero EOL padding are dropped before stream mutation.

rows.title: Mandatory MSS and segmentation
rows.behavior: GenOS emits a 20-byte TCP header and limits passive application sends to 128 bytes. Valid received MSS options pass structure checks but are not negotiated.
gaps: No advertised/negotiated MSS, path-dependent effective MSS or IPv6 TCP MSS. Structural MSS acceptance does not satisfy negotiation requirements.
planned: Test absent and small peer MSS on SYN, MSS emission, non-SYN options and payload-size bounds.

rows.title: Initial sequence and reincarnation
rows.behavior: Passive ISNs are deterministic tuple/peer-sequence XOR values. Local sequence arithmetic uses wrapping u32; it is not a secure ISN generator.
gaps: No clock/secret PRF ISN component, quiet-time or old-incarnation segment exclusion; entropy and long-session qualification remain open.
planned: Rapidly reuse the same tuple after close/reboot and inject retained segments; test a reviewed ISN generator.

rows.title: Connection establishment and passive ownership
rows.behavior: Active open and four tuple-keyed passive handshake cells exist; handshake ACKs require exact sequence and acknowledgment. Source address is the configured IPv4 address.
gaps: No simultaneous open or complete RFC state transition/previous-state model. Host predicate tests and the guest handshake do not cover every handshake anomaly.
planned: Script duplicate SYN/SYN-ACK, simultaneous open, early data/FIN and per-owner listener interference.

rows.title: Address and peer admission
rows.behavior: Inbound packets must name the configured destination and exact peer tuple. Socket connect validates zero addresses/ports; full broadcast/multicast/source-address policy is unqualified.
gaps: No complete invalid/broadcast/multicast OPEN/SYN campaign or general source-address selection.
planned: Exercise broadcast, multicast, zero and forbidden source/destination addresses at socket and wire boundaries.

rows.title: Close, half-close and TIME-WAIT
rows.behavior: Passive peer EOF and guest FIN/ACK have bounded state; post-EOF bytes and duplicate FIN do not redeliver. Reset/failure is reported and slots can be cancelled.
gaps: No 2MSL TIME-WAIT, complete simultaneous close/half-open recovery or long-lived tuple-retirement proof.
planned: Script both close directions, simultaneous close, lost final ACK and delayed old packets after slot/tuple reuse.

rows.title: Retransmission timing and Karn
rows.behavior: Passive sends skip ambiguous RTT samples after retransmission. RTO starts at 25 ticks, uses a bounded heuristic, backs off up to 100 ticks and fails after three attempts.
gaps: No SRTT/RTTVAR estimator, RFC second-scale floor/ceiling or complete per-state timer management. This bounded VM heuristic is not RFC 6298 conformance.
planned: Use a controllable clock for initial/first/subsequent RTT, Karn, earliest expiry, timer restart and repeated loss.

rows.title: Retry, idle and application failure
rows.behavior: Passive retry and idle lifetimes are finite; active compatibility paths use finite polls. Failed transport removes its slot and socket errors remain observable.
gaps: No configurable R1/R2 or three-minute SYN retry policy, negative route advice, or standardized soft/hard ICMP error report.
planned: Test independent R1/R2 thresholds, user abort, SYN persistence and failure/report cleanup.

rows.title: Optional keep-alive facility
rows.behavior: No keep-alive socket facility is advertised. The 200-tick passive idle deadline is a resource limit, not a keep-alive timer.
gaps: Keep-alive configuration and its conditional requirements have no implementation/test claim. Well-formed keep-alive probes are not malformed merely because the API is absent.
planned: If enabled, test default-off, configurable idle interval, probe shape and lost ACK tolerance.

rows.title: Urgent-data semantics
rows.behavior: The parser retains flags but not urgent-pointer semantics. There is no urgent-data delivery or application notification facility.
gaps: Mandatory urgent handling is missing; a valid URG segment is not classified as malformed. Absence is a conformance gap, not a satisfied optional exclusion.
planned: Test pointer interpretation, zero-window urgent handling, notification and queued-byte observation.

rows.title: Send/receive windows and updates
rows.behavior: Unsigned u16 windows cap one send flight; exact sequence/ACK window updates cannot complete another flight. Receive occupancy advertises zero and reopens after consumption.
gaps: No general window shrink/partial ACK/multiple-flight model, widened window scaling or urgent-at-zero handling.
planned: Test window shrink around SND.UNA, partial ACK, reordered updates and RST/URG while zero.

rows.title: Zero-window probing and resource lifetime
rows.behavior: Queued bytes stay owned while a peer window is zero. Bounded exponential probes do not advance data or count as congestion loss; the idle deadline eventually fails and releases the stream.
gaps: The fixed idle limit does not satisfy indefinite acknowledged zero-window persistence. No general persist lifetime or application-controlled resource-abort qualification.
planned: Separate indefinite valid zero-window behavior from an explicit user/resource abort and verify cleanup.

rows.title: Silly-window avoidance and Nagle
rows.behavior: Each bounded queued send can transmit immediately when no flight exists; small windows split that queue. No Nagle/SWS algorithm or disable option is advertised.
gaps: Small-window progress is not sender/receiver SWS or Nagle conformance.
planned: Test tiny writes, tiny receive increments, algorithm thresholds and explicit Nagle disable.

rows.title: ACKs, duplicate data and bounded reassembly
rows.behavior: Cumulative ACKs accompany admitted/repeated data; one deferred 128-byte segment preserves a gap and FIN. Conflicting partial overlaps keep the original bytes; reads never expose a gap.
gaps: No general multi-slot reassembly/merging, full ACK aggregation or delayed-ACK policy. The one-slot capacity is a profile limit, not malformed input.
planned: Test multiple gaps, legal larger segments, arbitrary overlap partitions and a bounded delayed-ACK timer.

rows.title: PUSH and application send policy
rows.behavior: Data flights set PSH/ACK and exact ACK completion retires the queued send. The fixed socket API does not expose separate PUSH or FLUSH controls.
gaps: No successive-PUSH coalescing or general send-max-segment policy/qualification.
planned: Test successive writes/PUSH boundaries, no indefinite buffering, and partial application send completion.

rows.title: Application interface, errors and Diffserv
rows.behavior: Owned handles expose send/receive, readiness, shutdown, close and failure. Requests retain exact owner/handle/incarnation identity; partial reads and backpressure are bounded.
gaps: No local-address OPEN parameter, Diffserv controls or full RFC error-report/FLUSH interface.
planned: Test defined local-address binding, error/report control and any future Diffserv/FLUSH options.

rows.title: IP TTL policy
rows.behavior: IPv4 emission uses a fixed TTL of 64.
gaps: No configurable TCP/application TTL interface or corresponding test.
planned: Test explicit TTL configuration and emitted header values.

rows.title: IPv4 option and routing interface
rows.behavior: IPv4 admission bounds IHL and validates its checksum; TCP option checks do not implement IPv4 routing options.
gaps: No source-route interface/return-route handling or IP option negotiation; structurally valid IP options are distinct from malformed IHL.
planned: Test valid unknown IP options separately from bad lengths/checksum, and any explicitly supported routing option.

rows.title: ICMP error delivery
rows.behavior: The current coordinator handles echo/control traffic; TCP has no complete typed ICMP error path.
gaps: No reviewed hard/soft ICMP error reporting, quoted-tuple validation or route advice. Source quench and other valid ICMP messages are not blanket malformed TCP.
planned: Inject correct/forged quoted tuples and verify non-aborting soft errors versus hard error policy.

rows.title: ECN and larger negotiated extensions
rows.behavior: ECN negotiation, window scale, timestamps, SACK and multipath are not advertised; structurally valid unknown TCP options are ignored.
gaps: No negotiated extension or related recovery/anti-wrap claim. Unsupported valid input must not become an invalid-format label.
planned: Test extension negotiation/decline and ordinary traffic after a valid unsupported offer.

rows.title: Reset/challenge ACK and injection defense
rows.behavior: An exact receive-sequence RST resets the passive stream; an in-window guess is challenged at most once per tick; foreign/out-of-window data cannot complete a flight.
gaps: The tests qualify bounded passive behavior, not all RFC 5961 states, global challenge budgets, secure ISNs or authenticated transport.
planned: Script SYN-RECEIVED/active-open RSTs, repeated same-tick challenge attempts and cross-owner attack budgets.

rows.title: Congestion control and alternate algorithms
rows.behavior: Passive timeout lowers the threshold and sets cwnd to one 128-byte MSS; exact ACK grows a capped cwnd. Each flight is bounded by both peer window and cwnd.
gaps: No full RFC 5681 algorithm qualification, multi-flight accounting, fast retransmit/recovery, byte-counted partial-ACK growth or idle restart. Named AIMD markers are not a conformance result.
planned: Use deterministic loss/duplicate-ACK/idle schedules with cwnd/ssthresh/flight invariants and baseline measurements.

rows.title: Bounded ownership, cancellation and concurrency
rows.behavior: Four global handshakes/streams and two per incarnation bound authority. Host tests cover exact request completion, sibling cancellation, exhaustion and slot reuse.
gaps: Two peers on one guest listener do not prove wire fairness across distinct process owners, reset quiescence or long-lived sessions.
planned: Run different process owners with one stalled/malicious peer, delayed completion and cancellation during device failure.

system_evidence.scope: Actual VirtIO/guest/host TCP exchange, two clients on one listener, selected loss/reorder/FIN and frozen budgets; not all RFC behavior.

followup: N1.2/N1.3/N1.4/N1.5 and SEC2 remain open; verified means only the exact declared behavior/tests, never whole-RFC conformance.
